children: Michael Burry is doubling down against some of the market's hottest AI and semiconductor trades, adding in some size to short positions in Micron Technology
The famed investor's September 22 Substack post suggests his concern is increasingly focused on whether today's semiconductor shortages, AI enthusiasm and elevated valuations can persist.
Micron sits at the center of that argument.

Burry highlighted comments from Acer CEO Jason Chen questioning expectations for a prolonged memory shortage. Chen acknowledged shortages in some products, including LPDDR5 and DDR5 9600, but offered a sharply different picture for DDR4.
No way! How could there be a continuous shortage? Chen said.
Burry also highlighted Chen's observation that DDR4 currently has more sellers than buyers, saying those comments align with his own view.

The implication is important for Micron investors. A sustained memory shortage can support pricing and margins, but rising supply relative to demand could eventually pressure both, challenging one of the key assumptions behind the current semiconductor cycle.

He described the Nasdaq 100 as historically overvalued and historically top-heavy as the index approached another record, while increasing bearish exposure to Palantir, Nebius and semiconductors broadly.
Yet Burry is not simply retreating from equities.

He also added to positions in QXO, Build-A-Bear Workshop, Sprouts Farmers Market, Birkenstock and MercadoLibre after what he described as tremendous corrections. He now considers all five full positions and their prices rather attractive.

title: Michael Burry Doubles Down Against Micron Stock
